findings.conclusion: The UI passes the complete eight-field draft through parseProblem and solveProblem; it does not implement a second solver. Table rows, optimal labels, slacks, pair decisions and observation downloads all read the same frozen result. Selecting a vertex changes only inspection.

Exact reduced fraction strings remain unchanged in tables, selected-vertex details, summaries and JSON. Number conversion occurs only inside SVG coordinate mapping. Point, segment, whole-region and empty outcomes retain their distinctions; the display never substitutes a numeric zero for infeasibility.

Input/change retires current result and disables observation download. A refused Apply retains entered fields but hides the old result and exposes an alert. Applying and rendering are synchronous, so no overlapping asynchronous calculation can restore stale authority. Preset replacement is explicit and immediately reapplies its complete fields.

Dynamic text is assigned using textContent. SVG values derive from bounded validated numbers and generated rational strings. Course and guide are embedded as base64 bytes. The builder fixes the UI import boundary, validates expected model exports, rejects closing-script text, and checks each template marker occurs once.

An independent source reconstruction reproduces the exact 64,651-byte HTML. Actual builder --check passes. Decoded course/guide bytes equal source files. The actual embedded course passes unchanged native parseDeck with 16 questions and five concepts. No learner model, deck parser, active session, persistence or answer handler is changed.

Course, guide and observation are explicit native button actions. Observation includes the admitted problem, complete result and selected vertex; it contains no learner answer/progress. Blob URLs are revoked after the request. The status accurately says requested and leaves save custody to the browser.

The plot includes a title and description describing the current optimum and coverage, with an exact-data table alternative. Native labeled inputs/selects/buttons, form submission, visible focus styling, live status/detail and alert semantics provide keyboard and assistive-technology paths. These are source conclusions; real rendered accessibility, keyboard behavior, print layout and completed downloads remain browser gates.

The retained original network-flow builder was read and its fixed-export/base64/single-file/check pattern is preserved. Original network-flow template and UI were absent from the retained baseline, so no byte-level comparison of those files is claimed.
